name: Avram Iancu Cluj International Airport
before:
Transylvania's airport, and the second busiest in Romania after Bucharest. It handled 3.24 million passengers in 2023, which for a regional airport is substantial, and it is the obvious arrival point for anything in the historic region rather than routing clients through the capital.

It is 9 km east of Cluj-Napoca, in the Somesheni area now inside the city limits, and the drive in takes about twenty minutes. Public transport is good for a city this size: trolleybus 8 runs to Mihai Viteazul Square in the centre, trolleybus 5 to the main railway station, and the A1E express runs from the airport exit into the square without stopping.

It sits on the European route E576 and close to the A3 Transylvania Motorway, so onward driving is straightforward.

The airport was originally Somesheni and is named after Avram Iancu, the Romanian revolutionary, so both names appear in older material.
after:
Transylvania's main airport, and the second busiest in Romania after Bucharest. It handled more than 3.5 million passengers in 2025, which for a regional airport is substantial, and it is the obvious arrival point for anything in the historic region rather than routing clients through the capital.

About 9 km east of the centre of Cluj-Napoca, it sits inside the city limits. The airport allows about 30 minutes for the drive in. Public transport is good for a city this size: line 8 runs to Mihai Viteazul Square in the centre and line 5 to the railway station, and the airport puts either ride at about 26 minutes.

The airport is named after Avram Iancu, though its own releases often shorten the name to Cluj International Airport, so expect to see both.

claims.note: Was 'Transylvania's airport'. Sibiu and Targu Mures also fly from Transylvania, so 'main' is added. The operator speaks of its position among the competing airports of the Transylvania region and calls itself the country's most important regional airport; Wikipedia calls it the most important airport in the historical region. Eurostat's 2025 table has Sibiu at 694,215 and Targu Mures at 151,124 against Cluj's 3,547,053.
